payload.body:
The way someone talks, listens, and disagrees matters a lot to how close you can become. The way another person thinks, listens, questions, and disagrees tells you a great deal about how close you can actually be, and you are often drawn to people who can tell you what they really think without making every difference feel dangerous.

Close relationships sharpen your thinking because another person gives you something real to respond to. They remember the situation differently, catch the detail you missed, or make an argument strong enough that you have to decide what you actually believe instead of repeating the first answer that came to mind.

A good explanation can carry more authority than it deserves. Someone can explain exactly why they behaved the way they did and still leave you living with the same behavior. You can understand their intentions, see their point, and know why the conversation went wrong without that understanding changing what you want from the relationship.

Words tell you what another person understands. What they do afterward tells you what the relationship can actually hold. You need enough honesty in the conversation to know what you think, what they think, and what both of you are willing to do with that information.
